subject: Pilot fellowship: request for pro-bono inference credits for student research
messages:
From: Dr. Helen Yang <helen.yang@eastbridge.edu>
To: rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2027 14:12:00 -0000
Subject: Request: pilot credits for undergraduate fellowship project

Hi Rishi,

I'm Helen, PI for the Cognitive Systems Lab at Eastbridge University. We're launching a paid undergraduate fellowship in fall term (8 students) to explore low-latency summarization for classroom transcripts. Our group is non-profit / academic and has limited cloud credits for this kind of compute.

We've used Redwood's hosted API in a small pilot and found the latency profile and streaming primitives a great fit. Before we start the full fellowship (late Sept), I wanted to ask if Redwood would consider providing a pro-bono pilot allocation (credits) or an educational discount to cover initial experimentation and evaluation for ~8 weeks. High-level ask: 200,000 tokens worth of generation + 10k embedding units (roughly ~USD 3k list).

Attached: short proposal (one page), IRB acknowledgement, and a budget worksheet. Purpose: course-aligned research, open dataset release (anonymized) and attribution to Redwood in paper acknowledgements.

Timing: classes start Sep 20; ideal provisioning window is Sep 13 - Sep 30.

Happy to provide any paperwork (institution letter, PI signature) or coordinate a short demo with the students.

Best,
Helen
Dr. Helen Yang
Assistant Professor, Cognitive Systems Lab
Eastbridge University

Subject: Re: Request: pilot credits for undergraduate fellowship project

Hi Helen — thanks for reaching out and for the clear proposal. This is the kind of academic pilot we love to support. I can operationally approve a small trial grant but need sign-off from our education credit committee (and confirmation on the scope). A few quick clarifying questions:

- Can you confirm the expected peak concurrent usage pattern (eg: how many students hitting the API at once)?
- Will the anonymized dataset be public and under what license? (we prefer CC-BY or similar)
- Do you need streaming responses + function calling enabled for the students (some lab assignments use streaming to update UI)?

I've looped in Monica (CS lead) and Marissa (sales manager) to expedite internal approvals. If it's helpful I can provision a short-term promo key pending final sign-off.

If you prefer a quick call, I'm available Wed 8/1 15:00-16:00 UTC (or Thurs morning).

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Vendor Partnerships | Redwood Inference

From: Dr. Helen Yang <helen.yang@eastbridge.edu>
To: rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com
Cc: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@eastbridge.edu>, Eastbridge Research Grants <grants@eastbridge.edu>
Date: Wed, 01 Sep 2027 11:22:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Request: pilot credits for undergraduate fellowship project

Hi Rishi — thanks for the fast reply. Answers below: 

- Peak concurrent: at most 6 students concurrently (the UI queues requests; typical bursts are 2–4).
- Dataset & license: We plan to release anonymized transcripts under CC-BY-SA 4.0. We'll redact PII and share the anonymization script with you for review if that helps.
- Streaming & function calling: Yes, we plan to use streaming for the real-time UI and a small function-calling hook to map structured metadata.

We can sign a simple MOU or an institutional letter; grants office is copied (they handle paperwork).

If you can provision a provisional key for the class start window and we'll follow up with paperwork, that would be perfect. We appreciate Redwood's consideration.

Best,
Helen
